answer.rationale: Primary supply lapses in 14 days with no auto-renew while the line is at 94% and has no buffer, so the single decision this cycle must preserve continuity. Incumbent already refused a price reopen, so negotiate_terms would likely spend the only slot and still leave expiry risk. add_second_source and defer_decision do not replace the expiring primary; memory_c5’s deferral was for non-critical month-to-month service, which this is not. switch_primary_vendor is the path that could cut unit cost (memory_c2) but would raise delivery risk in a no-buffer window and therefore fails the stated objective. memory_c1 is the only option that historically kept integration and deliveries intact. Verifying c1 and c2 before commit; 18% spend cut remains unmet and should be pursued next cycle. Downstream line-stoppage risk is material.
